title: IdentityDigestVectors
description: The pinned identity-digest protocol vectors (docs/IDENTITY_DIGEST.md). A consumer pins schema_version 1, implements the algorithm independently, and asserts the whole file: the digested `cases`, the `accepts` documents its ingress must let through, and the `rejections` it must refuse with the named rule at the named path. Reproducing the `cases` alone is not conformance. Each sha256 is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical form of its payload, computed by the reference implementation named in the document. A change to the algorithm, the digested field set or these vectors needs a new schema_version; a consumer fails closed on an unknown one.

accepts.description: Documents the ingress must accept: their number literals are spellings the protocol allows, and the payload parsed from the text digests to sha256. A guard that refuses one of these refuses what the protocol carries.

digests.description: Which subject the payload is: StateSnapshot content, DecisionProposal, or ExecutionIntent payload.

payload.description: The exact object that is digested. For a snapshot or proposal it is the contract's complete serialized form, so a consumer digests the payload it receives without adding, removing or normalizing a field. It is an object, not a document: how this file happens to spell a number inside one is not a spelling the ingress rule judges, which applies to `document` values.

document.description: Raw JSON document text the ingress must accept: every number literal in it denotes exactly the value it parses to. The payload parsed from this text must digest to sha256.

expect.description: Machine-readable: this document is never digested.

document.description: Raw JSON document text, because an out-of-domain, non-finite or only-rounding number cannot be carried in a JSON payload.

reason.description: The rule that must have refused the document: an integer outside the domain, a number with no finite value, or a literal that only rounds to the double it parses to.

path.description: JSON path of the refused literal; the refusal must name exactly this path.
